newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re sees Amer Re deal complete by end-Nov.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re sees Amer Re deal complete by end-Nov.

text.p: Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG, the world's largest reinsurer, said on Monday it expected to complete its takeover of American Re by the end of November.
The German group, known as Munich Re, had revealed plans in August to take over the third-ranked U.S. reinsurer American Re for $3.3 billion.
"We hope that we can complete the acquisition of American Re this month," Munich Re management board chairman Hans-Juergen Schinzler told a news conference.
"The unavoidable official process is running so far without any obstacles," he added.
Munich Re will not consolidate American Re until the 1997/1998 business year, however.

Schinzler also said that the Munich Re group, which has revealed two major acquisitions this year, was not planning any acquisitions this year in France, which it regards as a weak spot in its international business.
"We neither plan nor do we see any possibilities for a French acquisition," Schinzler said.
Schinzler added that Munich Re remained keen to strengthen its position in France, where it lags well behind rivals SCOR and Swiss Re.
As well as taking over American Re, Munich Re this year announced a takeover of Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG, the German health insurance group.
